subject: EU in-region access & lawful transfer — technical + SCCs Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Varga <elena.varga@medicorp-eu.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: medicorp-security@medicorp-eu.com
Date: Tue, 15 Oct 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: EU in-region processing and lawful transfer questions

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team ran a quick review and we have a handful of follow-up technical and contractual questions before we progress to legal sign-off: 

1) Can you confirm that all customer content (raw prompt + model outputs + KV cache) for our tenant will be processed and persisted only in EU regions (Frankfurt/Amsterdam)?
2) Does Redwood’s control plane ever store or process customer content outside the EU? If so, what metadata and for what purpose?
3) Are the EU SCCs executed between Medicorp and Redwood? We need a signed copy and a short attestation that no onward transfers occur without appropriate safeguards.
4) Retention and deletion — please state your default retention windows for: KV cache, inference logs, audit logs, backups. Also what deletion evidence you can provide (logs or cert).
5) Any US-person access to data? Which teams, what justifications, and what access controls/auditing exist?

If possible could you provide: a) the signed SCCs PDF, b) a simple network/dataflow diagram showing which components live in EU vs global, and c) a sample deletion/retention evidence extract.

We’d like to get this resolved this week — our legal and procurement teams are on standby.

Best,
Elena Varga
VP, Security & Privacy
Medicorp

Attachments: (none yet)

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varga <elena.varga@medicorp-eu.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Oct 2028 10:02:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: EU in-region processing and lawful transfer questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya (privacy lead) and Laura (legal) to confirm a few details and attach the formal materials. High-level answers below so you have immediate context: 

- In-region data plane: Yes — customer content (prompts, outputs, KV cache, model state) for Medicorp can be restricted to EU data centers (we support Frankfurt and Amsterdam regions).
- Control plane: Our control plane (management APIs, billing, and orchestration) is global by default and may include metadata that crosses regions for operational reasons. That metadata is limited — e.g., tenant id, timestamps, and non-content operational metrics. We can provide an architecture diagram and the exact fields that may be visible.
- SCCs and lawful transfer: Redwood executes EU SCCs with customers. Laura will share the signed SCC template and the short attestation language you requested.
- Retention/deletion: Default product windows are summarized below; Aditya will provide the canonical table and evidence artifacts: KV cache: ephemeral (kept up to 48 hours by default, configurable); Inference logs (token-level logs): 30–90 days depending on plan; Audit/trace logs: 90 days standard, longer by request.

Next steps I propose: 1) Aditya to post the signed SCCs + the EU dataflow diagram; 2) we schedule a 30-min call with your security and legal to walk the attestation language and DocuSign flow; 3) procurement thread for PO/contract.

Would morning CET tomorrow work for the call?

— Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (will follow)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varga <elena.varga@medicorp-eu.com>, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Oct 2028 10:32:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: EU in-region processing and lawful transfer questions

Elena, Monica — following up with the concrete artifacts and a few clarifications. See attached: SCCs_Redwood_signed.pdf and eu-data-flow.drawio.png (annotated). Key points below (technical + legal summary):

1) What we mean by "EU-only processing": data plane services (model runtime, persistent storage for model outputs and KV caches, and backups if you select EU-only) are pinned to EU regions. Our default hosted offering places tenant data in the region selected at onboarding.

2) Control plane / metadata: the control plane aggregates operational metadata necessary for routing and billing. The fields that may cross borders are limited to: tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, region_hint, and aggregated performance metrics. No prompt text, model outputs, or KV contents leave the EU unless you (a) explicitly enable a cross-region routing policy or (b) choose Hosted+Global tier for multi-region failover. We document the exact schema here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcdExampleEvidence

3) SCCs & transfers: Redwood signs the European Commission SCCs (Controller-Processor module) with customers; the attached PDF is the signed execution copy for Medicorp (redacted for public repo). The attestation language we can provide is a short statement confirming Redwood has executed SCCs and describing where and how transfers are performed. If you need additional contractual guarantees (e.g., Data Processing Addendum with specific audit rights), Laura can propose language.

4) Personnel access & auditing: US-based engineering may have emergency access to a subset of operational metadata under strict Just-In-Time approval, recorded in audit logs with SIEM hooks. Access is gated via RBAC + 2FA and requires an approved incident ticket; every access attempt logs the operator, reason, and time. We can export a sample access audit slice for your audit team.

5) Retention windows (default, but configurable in per-tenant settings):
   - KV cache: default 48 hours (can be reduced to 0 for stricter customers).
   - Inference logs: 30 days standard; 90 days on enterprise plans.
   - Audit/tracing logs: 90 days default; longer retention available as an add-on.
   - Backups: encrypted and stored in-region; standard retention 30 days unless configured otherwise.

6) Deletion evidence: we can provide a deletion event record (signed timestamped entry in our audit ledger) and a sample runbook extract showing deletion steps.

If Medicorp wants a deployment with zero control-plane metadata leaving the EU, recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — we’ll include an options matrix in the MAP.

Attached: SCCs_Redwood_signed.pdf (stub), eu-data-flow.drawio.png (diagram).

— Aditya Rao
Privacy & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SCCs_Redwood_signed.pdf; eu-data-flow.drawio.png

If you can attach the attestation + DocuSign-ready artifacts in this thread today, Medicorp procurement will prepare the PO and legal will route the DocuSign for signature. We’ll tentatively schedule a 30-min call tomorrow 09:30 CET to walk through final items.
